key_insight: Off-attractor supervision (OAS) retrains neural turbulence surrogates on states where they actually fail, helping them stay physically realistic instead of drifting, freezing, or blowing up.
engineering_relevance: For CFD surrogate deployment, OAS improves both short-term prediction and long-horizon statistical fidelity, making learned simulators more trustworthy beyond the training distribution.
method: Collect off-attractor states from surrogate rollouts, adversarial attacks, and targeted perturbations.
Run DNS offline once on each selected state to obtain the correct future trajectory.
Relabel the surrogate with these DNS futures so it learns dynamics from failure modes, not just training trajectories.
evidence_signal: On 128^3 turbulence, OAS raised the median time to failure from 21 to 721 steps and achieved the best step-15 error and long-horizon statistics among compared methods.
watch_item: The approach adds offline DNS relabeling and depends on how well the selected off-attractor states cover realistic failure modes during deployment.
paper_title: Staying on the Attractor: Supervising Neural Surrogates of 3D Turbulence Where They Leave It
